# upgrade-checklist.mdx

Source: https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer/blob/main/site/docs/upgrade-checklist.mdx

---
title: Upgrade checklist
description: One-page upgrade checklist for interactive teams and CI.
sidebar_position: 7
---

Use this page when you want a repeatable, low-risk upgrade runbook.

## Interactive team checklist

1. Update the global `al` CLI.
   - Homebrew: `brew upgrade conn-castle/tap/agent-layer`
   - Script: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer/releases/latest/download/al-install.sh | bash`
2. Confirm the installed version:
   ```bash
   al --version
   ```
3. Optional: pre-warm cache for offline or constrained runners:
   ```bash
   al upgrade prefetch --version X.Y.Z
   ```
4. Preview changes before any writes:
   ```bash
   al upgrade plan
   ```
5. Apply changes:
   ```bash
   al upgrade
   ```
6. Validate generated outputs and connectivity:
   ```bash
   al sync
   al doctor
   ```
7. If needed, restore a snapshot:
   ```bash
   al upgrade rollback --list
   al upgrade rollback <snapshot-id>
   ```

## CI checklist (managed updates only)

Use this when CI should apply managed template updates without memory/deletion changes:

```bash
al upgrade --yes --apply-managed-updates
al sync
al doctor
```

Only add these flags when intentionally applying those categories:

- `--apply-memory-updates` — apply updates to files under `docs/agent-layer/`
- `--apply-deletions` — delete unknown files under `.agent-layer/` and `docs/agent-layer/` **except** `.agent-layer/tmp/`
- `--apply-tmp-deletions` — destructively delete files under `.agent-layer/tmp/` (ephemeral agent run artifacts; not snapshotted, not rollback-restorable). Requires `--yes` and is independent of `--apply-deletions`.

:::warning Tmp deletions are destructive and not rollback-protected
`--apply-tmp-deletions` permanently removes everything under `.agent-layer/tmp/`. The pre-upgrade snapshot does **not** capture tmp content, so `al upgrade rollback <snapshot-id>` will not bring back deleted plans, reports, or scratch files. Use this flag only when you are sure CI does not host any in-progress agent artifacts you need to keep. See [Ephemeral artifacts under .agent-layer/tmp/](./reference#ephemeral-artifacts-under-agent-layertmp) for the full contract.
:::

## Shell quick paths (macOS/Linux)

### bash / zsh

```bash
brew upgrade conn-castle/tap/agent-layer || \
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer/releases/latest/download/al-install.sh | bash
al upgrade plan
al upgrade
```

### fish

```fish
brew upgrade conn-castle/tap/agent-layer; or \
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer/releases/latest/download/al-install.sh | bash
al upgrade plan
al upgrade
```

## Notes

- `.agent-layer/al.version` is required for supported usage.
- `al upgrade prefetch` is the recommended cache warm-up command for offline/air-gapped workflows.
- Snapshot IDs are JSON filename stems under `.agent-layer/state/upgrade-snapshots/` (run `al upgrade rollback --list` to discover them quickly).
- Snapshots intentionally exclude `.agent-layer/tmp/`. Rollback will not restore tmp files — if you have in-progress agent artifacts under tmp that must survive an upgrade, copy them out before running `al upgrade`.
- For policy guarantees and release migration rules, see [Upgrades](./upgrades).

---

# upgrades.mdx

Source: https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer/blob/main/site/docs/upgrades.mdx

---
title: Upgrades
description: Upgrade contract, compatibility guarantees, migration rules, and platform support.
sidebar_position: 6
---

This page is the canonical upgrade contract for Agent Layer.

It defines:
- upgrade event categories,
- compatibility guarantees,
- release-versioned migration rules,
- and the supported OS/shell capability matrix.

If guidance in other docs is shorter or summarized, this page is the source of truth.

## In this page

- [How to upgrade](#how-to-upgrade)
- [Upgrade event model](#upgrade-event-model)
- [Compatibility guarantees](#compatibility-guarantees)
- [Ephemeral artifacts and rollback scope](#ephemeral-artifacts-and-rollback-scope)
- [Migration rules by release](#migration-rules-by-release)
- [Documentation version retention and access](#documentation-version-retention-and-access)
- [OS and shell capability matrix](#os-and-shell-capability-matrix)
- [Commitment level and limitations](#commitment-level-and-limitations)
- [Upgrade checklist](./upgrade-checklist)

## How to upgrade

1. Update the global `al` CLI:
   - **Homebrew (macOS/Linux):** `brew upgrade conn-castle/tap/agent-layer`
   - **Script (macOS/Linux):** `curl -fsSL https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer/releases/latest/download/al-install.sh | bash`
2. Upgrade the repo: `al upgrade plan` then `al upgrade`.

For a full step-by-step runbook (interactive and CI), see the [upgrade checklist](./upgrade-checklist).

## Upgrade event model

Agent Layer classifies upgrade-impact changes into three categories:

| Category | Meaning | Expected user action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `safe auto` | Low-risk change that can be applied automatically without manual migration steps. | Usually none beyond normal verification (`al doctor`, test/lint workflow). |
| `needs review` | Change is likely safe but may interact with local customizations. | Review prompts/diffs and choose whether to apply updates. |
| `breaking/manual` | Change cannot be safely auto-migrated or may require explicit user decisions. | Follow release migration notes before proceeding. |

Qualification guidance:
- `safe auto`: formatting-only docs changes, additive defaults, or internal behavior fixes that do not require user input.
- `needs review`: template updates where local edits may conflict, workflow/instruction rewrites, generated file ownership boundary changes.
- `breaking/manual`: command/flag removals, required config schema moves, or behavior changes that require an explicit user-controlled migration step.

Breaking-change policy:
- Agent Layer uses clean breaks for breaking/manual changes. Removed commands/flags fail immediately in the target release.
- We document exact migration actions in release notes and migration guidance instead of keeping compatibility shims.

Current enforcement status:
- This model is the published contract and release-labeling policy.
- Automated enforcement in CLI flows is planned for a future release.

## Compatibility guarantees

Agent Layer follows a sequential release-line guarantee:

- Guaranteed path: upgrade from `N-1` to `N` release lines only.
- Example: `0.7.x` to `0.8.x` is guaranteed.
- Non-guaranteed path: skipping release lines (for example `0.6.x` to `0.8.x`).

What "guaranteed" means:
- We provide documented migration guidance for the guaranteed path.
- We classify known upgrade-impact changes using the event model on this page.
- We aim to keep `al upgrade` workflows predictable for that one-step path.

What it does not mean:
- It is not a guarantee that every repo custom state can be auto-migrated.
- It does not guarantee one-step upgrades for skipped release lines.

## Ephemeral artifacts and rollback scope

`.agent-layer/tmp/` is a scratch directory for agent run artifacts (plans, reports, scratch dumps). It is treated specially across the upgrade lifecycle:

- **Snapshots exclude tmp.** Pre-upgrade snapshots under `.agent-layer/state/upgrade-snapshots/` do not capture files under `.agent-layer/tmp/`. This keeps snapshot size bounded regardless of how much scratch state has accumulated.
- **Rollback does not restore tmp.** `al upgrade rollback <snapshot-id>` will not recreate any tmp file deleted during the upgrade. If you need to keep an in-progress agent artifact across an upgrade, copy it out of `.agent-layer/tmp/` first.
- **Tmp deletion is gated.** Interactive deletion requires a destructive double-confirm. Non-interactive deletion requires the dedicated `--apply-tmp-deletions` flag — `--apply-deletions` alone never touches tmp content. The interactive "delete all unknowns?" prompt is similarly scoped: it deletes everything **except** tmp, and the grouped tmp prompt always fires separately.

For full mechanics see [Ephemeral artifacts under .agent-layer/tmp/](./reference#ephemeral-artifacts-under-agent-layertmp) in the reference guide.

## Migration rules by release

Migration rules are published per release and versioned with docs/release notes.

| Target release | Supported source release lines | Event summary | Required manual actions | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v0.12.0` | `0.10.x`, `0.11.0` | `needs review`: Adds typed Antigravity model selection, configurable Agent Dispatch depth, repo-local Codex home opt-in, shared Codex TOML patching, provider turn-stop chimes, serialized sync writes, signed/notarized macOS binaries, binary Homebrew delivery, and new workflow skills. | Run `al upgrade plan` then `al upgrade`. The upgrade prompts for `agents.codex.local_config_dir`; choose `true` to keep repo-local Codex auth/session/log behavior under `.codex/`, or `false` to use Codex's normal global/project config layering. The upgrade also prompts for `notifications.chime`; choose `true` to enable provider turn-stop chimes, or `false` to keep them disabled. Re-run `al wizard` if you want to set an Antigravity model or change Agent Layer folder tracking. | Migration manifest moves `agents.antigravity.agent_specific.model` to `agents.antigravity.model`, sets `agents.codex.local_config_dir = false` by default for non-interactive upgrades, and sets `notifications.chime = false` by default for non-interactive upgrades. It preserves the `0.10.2` supported floor so unpinned legacy upgrades still discover Gemini-to-Antigravity source-agnostic migrations and v0.11.0 statusline defaults through the chained planner. When Codex local config is false or absent, Agent Layer preserves any inherited `CODEX_HOME` instead of setting or clearing it. |
| `v0.11.0` | `0.10.x` | `needs review`: Adds explicit opt-in provider statuslines for Claude Code and Codex. When enabled, Claude sync projects editable `.agent-layer/claude-statusline.sh` to `.claude/claude-statusline.sh` and wires `statusLine` in `.claude/settings.json`; Codex sync merges editable `.agent-layer/codex-statusline.toml` into `.codex/config.toml` unless `agents.codex.agent_specific.tui.status_line` is set. | Run `al upgrade plan` then `al upgrade`. The upgrade prompts for `agents.claude.statusline` and `agents.codex.statusline`; choose `true` to enable and seed any missing source file, or choose `false` to keep disabled. Claude's default statusline script requires `jq` on `PATH` at runtime. | Absent statusline keys mean disabled after v0.11.0. Migration manifest prompts write explicit true/false values. Missing enabled sources are seeded once; existing source files are user-owned, skipped by non-interactive upgrade, and replaced only after an interactive diff review. For unpinned legacy upgrades, the manifest also carries forward v0.10.2 Gemini->Antigravity source-agnostic operations until the known unpinned migration-chain issue is resolved. |
| `v0.10.2` | `0.10.x` | `safe auto`: Replaces Gemini CLI support and the retired Antigravity desktop launcher with Antigravity (`al agy`, `[agents.antigravity]`, repo-local `.agy/` config, and `agy --gemini_dir` containment). Adds `al probe agy` for observed permissions/MCP capability reporting. Removes `al gemini` entirely (no deprecation window); existing scripts must switch to `al agy`. Adds `.antigravitycli/` and `.agy/` to the gitignore template, keeps `/.gemini/` ignored for stale generated config safety, and stops generating `GEMINI.md`. Fresh installs default `[agents.antigravity] enabled = false`. Removes the Opus-only requirement for Claude `reasoning_effort`: a value set with a non-Opus or unset `agents.claude.model` now passes validation (Claude Code applies the effort where the active model supports it), and `al wizard` offers the reasoning-effort prompt for any enabled Claude model. | Run `al upgrade plan` then `al upgrade`. Existing `[agents.gemini] enabled = true/false` is migrated to `[agents.antigravity] enabled = true/false`; MCP server client lists are migrated from `gemini` to `antigravity`; stale Gemini `model` and `reasoning_effort` keys plus the retired Antigravity desktop table are removed (any pre-existing `[agents.antigravity]` enable flag from the retired desktop launcher is replaced by the migrated Gemini value or the default when legacy Gemini is present; current Antigravity enablement is preserved when no legacy Gemini table exists). Any stale `GEMINI.md` shim in the repo root is deleted (only when it carries the Agent Layer `GENERATED FILE` watermark; hand-authored files at that path survive). The upgrade snapshot captures the original. Run `al probe agy` after upgrade if you rely on Antigravity MCP behavior. | Migration manifest includes `config_delete_key` (`agents.antigravity`, gated for unknown-source upgrades unless legacy Gemini is present), `config_rename_key` (`agents.gemini.enabled` -> `agents.antigravity.enabled`), `config_replace_string` (`mcp.servers[].clients[]`: `gemini` -> `antigravity`), `config_delete_key` (`agents.gemini`), `config_set_default` (`agents.antigravity.enabled = false`), and `delete_generated_artifact` (`GEMINI.md`). As of v0.10.2 the agy v1.0.0 probe baseline writes and migrates Antigravity MCP config, but runtime MCP registration is not yet observed; re-check with `al probe agy` when upgrading agy. |
| `v0.10.1` | `0.10.x` | `safe auto`: Adds two new diff-scoped cleanup skills (`prune-new-tests`, `simplify-new-code`); renames `simplify-code` skill to `simplify-codebase` (full-repo scope) and removes the legacy directory; wires fresh-context reviewer subagents into `implement-plan`, `audit-and-fix-uncommitted-changes`, `verify-against-plan`, `address-pr-comments`, and `improve-codebase`; adds `al init --here` flag for in-place installs in subdirectories of existing repos; deep-merges Claude `agent_specific` configuration so `permissions.deny` is additive (arrays/scalars still replace); auto-writes a Codex per-repo `[projects."<repo root>"] trust_level = "trusted"` stanza to repo-local `.codex/config.toml`; ships `agent_specific.permissions.deny = ["AskUserQuestion"]` in the install seed so fresh `al init` disables Claude Code's clarification-question tool by default (existing repos unaffected); adds a human-gated merge phase to `ship-pr`. | Run `al upgrade plan` then `al upgrade`. The upgrade removes the legacy `.agent-layer/skills/simplify-code/` directory; if you customized that skill, back it up first. Existing repos do not inherit the new install-seed `permissions.deny = ["AskUserQuestion"]`; add it manually to `agents.claude.agent_specific.permissions.deny` if you want the new default. The Codex per-repo trust stanza is written to `.codex/config.toml` on next sync. | Migration manifest includes one `delete_file` operation (`.agent-layer/skills/simplify-code`). No config schema changes. Claude `agent_specific` object values are now deep-merged into `.claude/settings.json`; `permissions.deny` is additive and does not trigger an override warning. |

Migration execution rules for supported release-line upgrades:
- Each supported target release ships an embedded migration manifest at `internal/templates/migrations/<target>.json`, including `min_prior_version`.
- `al upgrade` executes migration operations before template writes and emits a deterministic migration report.
- If source version resolution fails, source-agnostic operations still run; source-gated operations are skipped and reported.
- `.agent-layer/.env` is namespace-scoped: only keys prefixed with `AL_` are loaded. Non-`AL_` keys are ignored and there is no env-key migration path.

How this table is maintained:
- Add or update a row for every release.
- If a release includes `breaking/manual` items, list exact required actions.
- If no special migration is needed, keep the row explicit to avoid ambiguity.

## Documentation version retention and access

Agent Layer website docs are versioned per release, then retained with a bounded policy to keep the published set stable and small:

1. Keep the newest 4 patch releases from the newest minor line.
2. Keep the newest patch release for each of the newest 4 minor lines (including the newest minor line).
3. Keep stable releases only (prereleases are dropped).
4. Keep the union of both sets in newest-first order.

How to access older docs:

1. Use the docs version selector in the website navigation to switch between retained versions.
2. If a version is not listed there, it has been pruned from the hosted site by retention policy.
3. For pruned versions:
   - Use the [Changelog](/changelog) for release-level historical behavior.
   - Browse source docs at the matching tag in the main repo:
     - `https://github.com/conn-castle/agent-layer/tree/vX.Y.Z/site/docs`

### Ownership baseline and manifest policy

Upgrade ownership classification is deterministic and offline:

- Release manifests are committed in-repo under `internal/templates/manifests/<version>.json`.
- Backfill manifests are committed for `v0.6.0`, `v0.6.1`, and `v0.7.0`.
- New releases must add a manifest for the new tag as part of release prep.
- Runtime upgrade planning does not call GitHub/tag APIs to infer ownership.

Repo-local baseline state is stored at:

- `.agent-layer/state/managed-baseline.json`

`al upgrade plan` compares local files against baseline evidence plus embedded manifests and emits `unknown_no_baseline` when ownership cannot be proven safely.

## OS and shell capability matrix

Windows is not supported.

| Surface | macOS | Linux | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Install via Homebrew | Supported | Supported | Requires Homebrew setup for platform. |
| Install via `al-install.sh` | Supported | Supported | Requires `curl` and `sha256sum` or `shasum`. |
| `al` CLI core commands | Supported | Supported | Includes `init`, `upgrade`, `sync`, `doctor`, client launch commands. |
| VS Code launchers | Supported | Supported | macOS: `.app`/`.command`; Linux: `.desktop`/`.sh`. |
| Shell completion: `bash` | Supported | Supported | `al completion bash --install`. |
| Shell completion: `zsh` | Supported | Supported | `al completion zsh --install`; may require `fpath` setup. |
| Shell completion: `fish` | Supported | Supported | `al completion fish --install`. |

## Commitment level and limitations

This contract is intended to be explicit without over-promising:

- We commit to best-effort adherence to this model and guarantee scope.
- If we cannot fully meet a guarantee in a specific release, we will document the limitation clearly in release notes and migration guidance.
- When in doubt, prefer explicit communication over silent assumptions.
